# 10:10 Breakout on BankNifty Options — Methodology, Pre-Committed 2026-07-27 Before Any Result Exists

## Why this exists

Candidate 15 in this project's strategy search (see `quantos_dow_theory_trend_status`
memory for candidate 14 and the running count). Second of 5 unsourced retail
day-trading ideas the user brought 2026-07-26 — same low-rigor category as
candidate 14 (Dow theory) and the Iron-Condor CSV this project already
debunked once; picked next because its data blocker (`_fyers_symbol()`, see
`docs/DOW_THEORY_TREND_METHODOLOGY.md`) is now fixed.

**Do not edit this file after the backtest has run.** A wrong parameter is a
finding for a NEXT pre-registered run, not a retroactive edit here.

## The source strategy

5-minute BankNifty chart. The 12th candle of the day (opens 10:10 IST, the
window 10:10–10:15) is the reference candle. If a later candle's price
crosses **above** that candle's high → enter a CALL; crosses **below** its
low → enter a PUT. Stop loss capped at 40 index points, target up to 200
index points. One trade per day (first breakout only).

## The central limitation, stated up front — this is a synthetic-premium backtest

`docs/CANDIDATE15_OPTION_DATA_FEASIBILITY.md` confirmed 2026-07-27: **Fyers
has no historical intraday data for any expired option contract**, at any
age (checked 6 days to 30 months post-expiry, both illiquid and 48.8M-volume
contracts). There is no way to fetch a real traded option premium path for
this backtest. **Every premium value in this backtest is a Black-Scholes
theoretical price**, computed from real BankNifty index levels and a real
India VIX-derived IV input — not a real traded/settled price.

This is a materially different, weaker form of validation than every prior
options candidate in this project. The VRP candidate
(`docs/VRP_METHODOLOGY.md`) priced trades off real NSE bhavcopy settle
prices; this one cannot. A pass here would show the **index-level signal
timing has edge net of a theoretically-modeled cost path** — it would NOT
show that the real option market would have paid out that way (real
bid-ask spread, skew/smile deviation from Black-Scholes fair value, and
fill slippage on both legs are all unmeasured and unmeasurable from this
data). **A pass on this backtest is not sufficient on its own to move to
live capital** — it would need a follow-up feasibility check against real,
current option chain quotes before that step, disclosed here rather than
deferred silently.

**Window: 2021-06-01 through the latest available session**, re-verified at

## Contract selection — monthly-only, a disclosed simplification

BankNifty has traded **monthly-only** options since Nov-2024 (weeklies
discontinued); before that it also had weeklies, in a symbol format this
backtest does not attempt to construct. **This backtest always uses the
nearest calendar-month contract, for the entire window**, not just the
post-2024 portion — a deliberate simplification, not an oversight: it
avoids the weekly-symbol-format ambiguity entirely and keeps the contract
selection rule identical (and therefore comparable) across the whole tested
period, at the cost of using a contract with more residual time value (and
correspondingly lower gamma/theta sensitivity to the 40pt/200pt intraday
move) than a trader would realistically pick when a nearer weekly existed.
**Strike**: nearest 100-point strike to the BankNifty index level at the
moment of entry (ATM at entry, not re-struck if price runs).

## Session definition

Regular NSE session, 09:15–15:30 IST (03:45–10:00 UTC). **Flatten any open
position by 15:20 IST** (09:50 UTC, at that bar's close) — same square-off
buffer as candidate 14.

## Reference candle and breakout signal

The 12th 5-minute candle of the day (open 10:10 IST, close 10:15 IST,
1-indexed from the 09:15 candle) is the **reference candle** — its
`(high, low)` on the BankNifty index series are the breakout levels.
Unavailable (and no signal possible) on any day with fewer than 12 candles
before 10:10 (e.g. a shortened session) — such days are skipped, not
approximated with a shorter window.

From the 13th candle onward, on **candle close** (not intrabar wick touch —
same no-same-bar, no-intrabar-noise discipline as candidate 14's fractal
breakouts):
- `close > reference.high` → **CALL** signal (first occurrence only).
- `close < reference.low` → **PUT** signal (first occurrence only).
- Whichever direction fires first is the day's only trade — once fired, no
  further signals are evaluated that day (**one trade per day**, matching
  the source strategy exactly, unlike candidate 14's multi-trade design).
- A day with neither breakout by 15:20 IST has no trade.

**Execution**: at the **open of the next candle** after the signal candle's
close — same no-same-bar-execution discipline as every prior candidate.

## Stop and target — index points, both capped, mechanical tie-break

At entry (index level `E`, from the execution candle's open):
- `stop_distance = min(40, reference.high - reference.low)` index points
  (the source strategy's own "cap the stop at 40 because I don't want to
  check if the candle is 40 or 50 points," applied literally).
- `target_distance = 200` index points (fixed, not conditional on candle
  range — the source material never conditions the target the way it
  conditions the stop).
- **CALL**: stop level `= E - stop_distance`, target level `= E +
  target_distance`.
- **PUT**: stop level `= E + stop_distance`, target level `= E -
  target_distance` (inverted — a PUT profits from the index falling).

From the execution candle onward, each subsequent candle's `(high, low)` is
checked against both levels. **If both are crossed within the same candle,
the stop is assumed to have triggered first** — a standard conservative
tie-break (no tick data exists to resolve the true intrabar order),
disclosed now rather than picked after seeing which choice helps the
result. Whichever level is reached — stop, target, or neither by 15:20 IST
(session flatten) — sets the **exit index level** and exit timestamp.

## Premium reconstruction — Black-Scholes, contemporaneous VIX, both legs

At entry: `compute_greeks(spot=E, strike=ATM, days_to_expiry=(expiry -
entry_date).days, implied_vol=<India VIX 5m close at the entry candle's own
timestamp> / 100, option_type=CALL_or_PUT).theoretical_price` is the entry
premium.

At exit: same call, with `spot` = the exit index level (from whichever
trigger fired) and `implied_vol` = the India VIX 5m close **at the exit
candle's own timestamp** (not held flat from entry) — the VIX path during
the trade is real data already being fetched for the signal window, so
using it at both ends is a strictly more realistic choice than freezing a
single entry-time snapshot, at no extra data cost.

`days_to_expiry` is computed to the day, not the minute — because every
trade in this design opens and closes within the same session, entry and
exit `days_to_expiry` are almost always numerically identical, meaning
**intraday theta decay between entry and exit is not modeled** by this
reconstruction. Disclosed as a limitation, not a bug: for a monthly
contract (the only kind this backtest ever selects, see above) with
typically 5–35 calendar days of remaining life, intraday theta over a
trade lasting minutes to a few hours is genuinely small relative to the
40pt/200pt move sizes this strategy targets — a materially different (and
more defensible) claim than it would be for a 0–1 DTE weekly, which this
design deliberately never selects.

**India VIX is a NIFTY volatility index, not a BankNifty one** — using it as
BankNifty's IV proxy is a disclosed cross-asset basis assumption (the user's
explicit choice over a regime-conditioned or flat-IV alternative, 2026-07-27),
not a claim that the two are identical. No basis correction factor is
applied — a raw `VIX / 100` is used directly as the IV input.

## Position sizing — 1 lot per trade

BankNifty lot size = 30 (bhavcopy-confirmed, current). This strategy's own
description has no scale-out mechanic (unlike candidate 14) — it is a
single-shot day trade, stop or target, nothing in between. **1 lot per
trade**, the simplest literal implementation; no notional-matching exercise
the way candidate 14 needed one.

## Cost model — options buy-to-open / sell-to-close, reused rate schedules

A new function, `core/breakout1010/costs.py`, composes existing pieces
rather than rebuilding them: `core/risk/costs.py`'s `CostModel.round_trip()`
(the buy/sell-leg mechanics — STT on the sell leg, stamp duty on the buy
leg, brokerage/exchange/SEBI/GST on both, all direction-agnostic) is
structurally exactly this trade's shape (buy an option, sell it same day),
but its **default rates are NSE cash-equity rates**, wrong for F&O options.
Instantiated per-trade instead with the options-specific, time-varying
rates already sourced for the VRP candidate
(`core/options/vrp/costs.py`'s `stt_sell_rate(date)` — 0.0625% until
2024-09-30, 0.1% from 2024-10-01, 0.15% from 2026-04-01 — and
`EXCHANGE_TXN_PCT = 0.0003503`, NSE's Rs35.03/lakh F&O rate). Stamp duty
(0.003%, buy leg) and SEBI/GST rates are the same across cash and F&O
segments, so `CostModel`'s own defaults apply unchanged there.

## Validation criterion / pass-fail bar

**Same bar used throughout this project**: `core/backtest/parser.py`'s
`has_positive_edge` — profit factor > 1.0 AND Sharpe > 0.5 — on the pooled
NET (post-cost) trade set.

**Reported alongside the pooled number**: a per-year breakdown (2021
partial, 2022–2025, 2026 partial), same discipline as every prior
candidate.

## What would make this validation untrustworthy after the fact

- Changing the stop cap (40pt), target (200pt), the same-close (not
  intrabar) breakout rule, the stop-wins-on-same-candle tie-break, or the
  contemporaneous-VIX (vs entry-frozen) choice after seeing a weak or
  strong result.
- Switching from monthly-only contract selection to a weekly-aware one only
  for the pre-2024 portion of the window if the monthly-only result looks
  weak, rather than as a planned, disclosed-in-advance robustness check.
- Treating a pass on this backtest as sufficient to move to live capital
  without the real-option-chain follow-up check named above.
- Reporting only the pooled result while omitting the per-year breakdown.
